claims.text: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 18.2 km against a booked optimal of 14.0 km, an excess of 4.2 km — 30.0% of optimal — so both POL-RD-01 tests pass: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing field, so the same 18.2 km appearing on the trip record is not cited for the threshold test. Disclosure: the trace is impaired, weight_multiplier 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW, and the following claims deal with that impairment rather than hide it.

The one impairment cannot absorb the excess. It is a single 100.0 s sampling gap (19:39:44 to 19:41:24) whose bounding fixes are 1.01 km apart, on a trace with 94.5% coverage, 174 fixes and 30.3 minutes of running. POL-RD-07(i) requires the impaired stretch to be read as the straight line between its bounding fixes — the reading most favourable to the driver — and a 1.01 km stretch cannot account for a 4.2 km excess. The gap changes how one stretch is measured; it does not change whether a deviation exists.

The impaired trace does not stand alone. POL-RD-07(ii) allows a deviation to be corroborated by a counterparty_statement admitting the route, and the driver's own statement on this dispute, filed by the DRIVER on 2026-08-19, is 'Navigation rerouted me.' That is the counterparty admitting the vehicle did not follow the planned route — an account independent of the trace, never withdrawn and never qualified. The rider does not rely on trip_record.actual_distance_km for this purpose, because POL-RD-01 identifies it as a rounded convenience copy of the same trace measurement and therefore not independent. The corroboration POL-RD-07(ii) requires is present, and the trace's impairment (weight 0.6, issue GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW) is cured by it.

No traffic advisory excuses the excess. POL-RD-03 exonerates only against a traffic_advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching it, and is matched by a route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after. EV-ADVIS-02826-01 is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload — and its own issue detail records that no advisory covers the Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd corridor in this window. The absence is itself citable: with no advisory on file the comparison cannot be run and POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record.

The driver's explanation discharges nothing. Once the rider has shown a threshold-meeting excess, POL-RD-08 puts the burden on the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; 'Navigation rerouted me' names no advisory, no road and no evidence ID, so it carries no weight. POL-RD-13 requires such an assertion to be tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, and because no advisory identifier is cited, the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it — so this is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The driver is left with an unexplained 4.2 km.

No rider-caused detour can be made out. POL-RD-04 exonerates only to the extent of a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor or no more than three minutes after, and specific enough to act on. The chat log for TRP-02826 is COMPLETE and contains 0 messages, and trip_record.chat_message_count is 0, so there is no instruction, no waypoint_hint and nothing to corroborate. The rider asked for no detour and accepts none of the excess.

The baseline has not moved. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip record, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so no re-quote under POL-RD-05 exists and none may be derived; the booked 14.0 km optimal route is the correct baseline against which the trace is measured.

The pooled-trip baseline does not apply. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is not in play and measuring excess against the booked 14.0 km optimal is the correct field. The rider's claim does not fail on a wrong-field ground.

This is a metered trip, so the distance-refund route stays open. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs the computation. The rider is not asking for money she never lost on a fixed price; she is asking for the difference between what was charged and what the optimal route costs.

On POL-RD-02 the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 19.0) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, = 20.42; there is no ERP on the optimal route, no surcharge and no waiting-time fee to add. charged_total is 26.73, so the refund is 26.73 - 20.42 = 6.31, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as 6.35. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor, and at 23.6% of charged_total it is far below the 90% share that would convert it into a FULL_REFUND — so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.35 to the rider.

No pass-through charge may be added on top. POL-RD-09(1) forbids stacking off-route ERP on the POL-RD-02 figure, and nothing is due in any event: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00 and airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. The 6.35 is the distance and time difference alone, and no line of the ledger is counted twice.

The rider's initial burden is discharged. TRP-02826 is the trip identifier carried on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, the pickup timestamp matches across them, and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold. The rider's own profile raises no corroboration bar: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition of four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated is not met, and in any event the measured excess of 30.0% is not below 30%. (EV-GPS-02826 is impaired at weight 0.6, issue GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW, and is cited here only for the excess it measures.)

Only the profile counters the policy names may ground a finding. The driver's prior_deviation_flags (1) and prior_no_show_flags (2) are lifetime counters and near-synonyms of the trailing-window fields the clauses actually name, and substituting one for the other is forbidden by POL-GEN-01; rating, account age and cancellation rate on either profile are context only. The rider seeks no finding from any profile field, and none of them decides this trip — the trace and the ledger do.

Even on the least favourable reading, the rider does not end up carrying the disputed charge. If the panel were to hold that the impaired trace has no independent corroboration, POL-RD-10(3) governs and the ruling is ESCALATE: terminal, no monetary outcome, and the disputed amount held rather than collected under POL-GEN-03. The primary case is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 6.35; the alternative holds the money. Neither leaves the rider paying for 4.2 km she did not travel.

Relief can execute on issue. The monetary effect of 6.35 does not exceed the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, and neither dispute.safety_flag nor dispute.complaint_flag is set on this dispute, so the ruling is not held back for the human queue and the refund to the rider issues automatically.

claims.text: The GPS trace is impaired for policy purposes and cannot carry this deviation on its own. EV-GPS-02826 shows a 100.0 second gap between consecutive fixes (19:39:44 to 19:41:24) against an expected 10 second sampling interval, which exceeds the 90 second limit in POL-RD-07(a), and the admissibility pre-pass tags the artifact IMPAIRED with weight 0.6 under issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW ('GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW', MAJOR). I disclose that impairment and rely on it: under POL-RD-07 the deviation may not be established on this trace alone, and under POL-GEN-02(1) and (3) the weight and the issue codes must be named in any ruling that touches it.

None of the independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names exists in this bundle. The chat log carries zero messages (EV-CHAT-02826), so there is no driver admission to place the vehicle off the optimal corridor; the fare breakdown records no ERP gantries at all and 0.00 of tolls (EV-FARE-02826), so no charged crossing corroborates the route; and the 18.2 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02826) is, by POL-RD-01's own terms, a rounded convenience copy of the same trace measurement that may not be cited for the threshold test, so it is not a source the platform derived independently of this trace. With the trace impaired under POL-RD-07(a) and no corroboration, POL-RD-07(iii) directs ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, because the absence of proof here is a data failure and not a finding for the driver.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must measure an excess either from an unimpaired GPS trace or, where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), from an independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii). Limb (a) is met - TRP-02826 matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown - but limb (b) is not: the only excess figure in the bundle (4.2 km, 30.0%) is produced by the impaired trace itself, and the rider points to no POL-RD-07(ii) source. The burden never shifts to the driver, and the rider's claim is not sustained on this record.

The driver's one-line statement that 'navigation rerouted me' is not the 'counterparty_statement admitting the route' that POL-RD-07(ii) contemplates. It names no road, junction or segment; it does not place the vehicle on any identified corridor the optimal route does not use; and it was submitted on 19 August 2026, two days after the trip ended on 17 August and after the rider filed on 18 August. It supplies no route content, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion that points to no artifact discharges nothing.

EV-ADVIS-02826-01 is MISSING: its payload is null, its weight is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, recording that no advisory covers the Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd corridor in this window. Its absence is itself citable, and it is decisive in one narrow respect: under POL-RD-13 a traffic or navigation explanation is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, so with no advisory on file POL-RD-03 cannot be run in either direction. Neither an exculpation under POL-RD-03 nor a corroborated deviation is available on this record, and the case cannot be closed with a monetary finding.

Even though the evidence here is finely balanced enough to warrant the POL-RD-06 profile check, no pattern is established and none may be built. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 287, so neither the 3-flag test nor the 5% test is met on the two fields POL-RD-06 names. driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags (= 1) is a lifetime counter and is expressly NOT the trailing-90-day figure; POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting it. No balance is resolved against the driver, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available under POL-RD-06(b), and no conduct referral arises under POL-RD-06(c).

In the alternative - if the Judge were to establish a deviation despite the impaired trace - the measured excess of 4.2 km and 30.0% clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate but sits below both material gates (50% and 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift is unavailable and the remedy is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic alone. On the fare breakdown's own figures that arithmetic gives charged_total 26.73 less a recomputed_fare of 20.42, i.e. 6.31 before rounding and 6.35 payable, which is well under 90% of the charged total. The 11.00 the rider contests is not supported by any line of the record and no FULL_REFUND is reached on any view.

The payment state is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 the two outcomes this record supports are party-relative and both leave the fare in place: NO_ACTION preserves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand, and ESCALATE holds the disputed amount rather than collecting or refunding it. Only FULL_REFUND or PARTIAL_REFUND would take money out of the fare, and neither is available on an uncorroborated, impaired trace.

No billing-integrity or pass-through correction can be carved out of this fare on the rider's behalf. The fare breakdown reconciles to the 26.73 charged: erp_gantries is empty, tolls and ERP are 0.00, the airport surcharge line is 0.00, the platform fee is 0.80, and there is no charge line for a gantry the trace never crosses and no surcharge on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is nothing to refund under POL-RD-09(4), and no standalone pass-through correction exists to add to any distance refund.

To the rider and the driver: I cannot close this case with a payment, and it goes to a human reviewer. The reason is narrow, and it is about the quality of the one measurement the case turns on, not about who is telling the truth.

What the record shows. The ride ran 18.2 km against a booked optimal of 14.0 km — an excess of 4.2 km, or 30.0% of optimal — so both POL-RD-01 tests (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km) are met on the face of the figures. The fare charged was SGD 26.73 (EV-FARE-02826). Had the optimal route been driven, POL-RD-02 recomputes the fare as (3.80 + 0.75 × 14.0 + 0.28 × 19.0) × the fare-breakdown surge multiplier of 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee = SGD 20.42, a difference of SGD 6.31, payable SGD 6.35 after rounding up to the nearest 5 cents. I record those three figures — charged_total 26.73, recomputed_fare 20.42, refund 6.35 — even though no refund issues today, because they are the sums a reviewer will work from. The trip is metered, not upfront-quoted, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and this is the right arithmetic.

Why the money is held instead. EV-GPS-02826 contains a 100-second gap between fixes (19:39:44 to 19:41:24) against a 10-second sampling interval, and is graded IMPAIRED at weight 0.60 with issue GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW. That is also impairment for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a), so the deviation may not rest on the trace alone. The driver's statement, 'Navigation rerouted me', is a counterparty statement admitting the vehicle was rerouted, and I accept it as the independent corroboration POL-RD-07(ii) allows, so POL-RD-07(iii) does not by itself force escalation. But corroboration that a reroute happened does not repair the distance measurement: the 4.2 km excess is carried by EV-GPS-02826 at weight 0.60, and nothing else carries it independently. The 18.2 km on the trip record is, by POL-RD-01's own terms, a rounded copy of the same trace measurement that may not be cited for the threshold test; the fare ledger's distance comes from the same trace; and a counterparty statement carries no weight_multiplier, so it can neither lower nor raise the cap. Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence cannot exceed 0.60, which is below the 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) requires a human reviewer. If the driver's statement were read as too thin to corroborate, POL-RD-10(3) would require escalation on the same facts. Either way the disputed SGD 11.00 is held rather than collected or refunded.

The parties' other points. The driver's traffic explanation carries no weight: no traffic advisory covers this trip (EV-ADVIS-02826-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0), and POL-RD-13 tests such an explanation against the advisory and nothing else; because the driver named no advisory ID, the gap in the bundle is not by itself a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The rider's position is otherwise sound on the facts: the chat log holds no messages (EV-CHAT-02826), so POL-RD-04 finds no rider instruction, and no pickup or dropoff was amended, so POL-RD-05 leaves the 14.0 km baseline untouched. RYDE_X is not a pooled product, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. Nothing falls to be corrected under POL-RD-09 — no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge — and there is no billing-integrity finding. No repeat-deviation pattern is established (0 deviation flags over 287 completed trips in the last 90 days), so there is no POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. Neither profile decides anything: POL-GEN-01 permits only the trailing-window counters the clauses name, and the lifetime counters (prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags) are context only. POL-GEN-05 does not arise, because with no monetary effect there is nothing to execute.

What would resolve it. A measurement of this trip that does not depend on the 0.60-weight trace: a continuous GPS export covering 19:39:44 to 19:41:24, or a platform-derived distance or ERP gantry record that is not copied from this trace. On that evidence the SGD 6.35 (or the correct figure) can be ruled. Until then the fare stands as charged and the case goes to human review under POL-RD-10.

EV-ADVIS-02826-01 is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload — and its own issue detail records that no advisory covers the Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd corridor in this window. The absence is itself citable: with no advisory on file the comparison cannot be run and POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record.

The driver's explanation discharges nothing. Once the rider has shown a threshold-meeting excess, POL-RD-08 puts the burden on the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; 'Navigation rerouted me' names no advisory, no road and no evidence ID, so it carries no weight. POL-RD-13 requires such an assertion to be tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, and because no advisory identifier is cited, the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it — so this is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The driver is left with an unexplained 4.2 km.

ledger.claim: No rider-caused detour can be made out. POL-RD-04 exonerates only to the extent of a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor or no more than three minutes after, and specific enough to act on. The chat log for TRP-02826 is COMPLETE and contains 0 messages, and trip_record.chat_message_count is 0, so there is no instruction, no waypoint_hint and nothing to corroborate. The rider asked for no detour and accepts none of the excess.

The baseline has not moved. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip record, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so no re-quote under POL-RD-05 exists and none may be derived; the booked 14.0 km optimal route is the correct baseline against which the trace is measured.

The pooled-trip baseline does not apply. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is not in play and measuring excess against the booked 14.0 km optimal is the correct field. The rider's claim does not fail on a wrong-field ground.

This is a metered trip, so the distance-refund route stays open. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs the computation. The rider is not asking for money she never lost on a fixed price; she is asking for the difference between what was charged and what the optimal route costs.

On POL-RD-02 the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 19.0) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, = 20.42; there is no ERP on the optimal route, no surcharge and no waiting-time fee to add. charged_total is 26.73, so the refund is 26.73 - 20.42 = 6.31, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as 6.35. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor, and at 23.6% of charged_total it is far below the 90% share that would convert it into a FULL_REFUND — so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.35 to the rider.

No pass-through charge may be added on top. POL-RD-09(1) forbids stacking off-route ERP on the POL-RD-02 figure, and nothing is due in any event: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00 and airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. The 6.35 is the distance and time difference alone, and no line of the ledger is counted twice.

The rider's initial burden is discharged. TRP-02826 is the trip identifier carried on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, the pickup timestamp matches across them, and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold. The rider's own profile raises no corroboration bar: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition of four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated is not met, and in any event the measured excess of 30.0% is not below 30%. (EV-GPS-02826 is impaired at weight 0.6, issue GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW, and is cited here only for the excess it measures.)

Only the profile counters the policy names may ground a finding. The driver's prior_deviation_flags (1) and prior_no_show_flags (2) are lifetime counters and near-synonyms of the trailing-window fields the clauses actually name, and substituting one for the other is forbidden by POL-GEN-01; rating, account age and cancellation rate on either profile are context only. The rider seeks no finding from any profile field, and none of them decides this trip — the trace and the ledger do.

ledger.claim: Even on the least favourable reading, the rider does not end up carrying the disputed charge. If the panel were to hold that the impaired trace has no independent corroboration, POL-RD-10(3) governs and the ruling is ESCALATE: terminal, no monetary outcome, and the disputed amount held rather than collected under POL-GEN-03. The primary case is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 6.35; the alternative holds the money. Neither leaves the rider paying for 4.2 km she did not travel.

ledger.claim: Relief can execute on issue. The monetary effect of 6.35 does not exceed the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, and neither dispute.safety_flag nor dispute.complaint_flag is set on this dispute, so the ruling is not held back for the human queue and the refund to the rider issues automatically.

The GPS trace is impaired for policy purposes and cannot carry this deviation on its own. EV-GPS-02826 shows a 100.0 second gap between consecutive fixes (19:39:44 to 19:41:24) against an expected 10 second sampling interval, which exceeds the 90 second limit in POL-RD-07(a), and the admissibility pre-pass tags the artifact IMPAIRED with weight 0.6 under issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW ('GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW', MAJOR). I disclose that impairment and rely on it: under POL-RD-07 the deviation may not be established on this trace alone, and under POL-GEN-02(1) and (3) the weight and the issue codes must be named in any ruling that touches it.

None of the independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names exists in this bundle. The chat log carries zero messages (EV-CHAT-02826), so there is no driver admission to place the vehicle off the optimal corridor; the fare breakdown records no ERP gantries at all and 0.00 of tolls (EV-FARE-02826), so no charged crossing corroborates the route; and the 18.2 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02826) is, by POL-RD-01's own terms, a rounded convenience copy of the same trace measurement that may not be cited for the threshold test, so it is not a source the platform derived independently of this trace. With the trace impaired under POL-RD-07(a) and no corroboration, POL-RD-07(iii) directs ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, because the absence of proof here is a data failure and not a finding for the driver.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must measure an excess either from an unimpaired GPS trace or, where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), from an independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii). Limb (a) is met - TRP-02826 matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown - but limb (b) is not: the only excess figure in the bundle (4.2 km, 30.0%) is produced by the impaired trace itself, and the rider points to no POL-RD-07(ii) source. The burden never shifts to the driver, and the rider's claim is not sustained on this record.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-02826 at weight_multiplier 0.6 but does not name its issue code(s): GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW

ledger.claim: The driver's one-line statement that 'navigation rerouted me' is not the 'counterparty_statement admitting the route' that POL-RD-07(ii) contemplates. It names no road, junction or segment; it does not place the vehicle on any identified corridor the optimal route does not use; and it was submitted on 19 August 2026, two days after the trip ended on 17 August and after the rider filed on 18 August. It supplies no route content, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion that points to no artifact discharges nothing.

EV-ADVIS-02826-01 is MISSING: its payload is null, its weight is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, recording that no advisory covers the Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd corridor in this window. Its absence is itself citable, and it is decisive in one narrow respect: under POL-RD-13 a traffic or navigation explanation is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, so with no advisory on file POL-RD-03 cannot be run in either direction. Neither an exculpation under POL-RD-03 nor a corroborated deviation is available on this record, and the case cannot be closed with a monetary finding.

Even though the evidence here is finely balanced enough to warrant the POL-RD-06 profile check, no pattern is established and none may be built. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 287, so neither the 3-flag test nor the 5% test is met on the two fields POL-RD-06 names. driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags (= 1) is a lifetime counter and is expressly NOT the trailing-90-day figure; POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting it. No balance is resolved against the driver, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available under POL-RD-06(b), and no conduct referral arises under POL-RD-06(c).

ledger.claim: In the alternative - if the Judge were to establish a deviation despite the impaired trace - the measured excess of 4.2 km and 30.0% clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate but sits below both material gates (50% and 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift is unavailable and the remedy is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic alone. On the fare breakdown's own figures that arithmetic gives charged_total 26.73 less a recomputed_fare of 20.42, i.e. 6.31 before rounding and 6.35 payable, which is well under 90% of the charged total. The 11.00 the rider contests is not supported by any line of the record and no FULL_REFUND is reached on any view.

ledger.claim: The payment state is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 the two outcomes this record supports are party-relative and both leave the fare in place: NO_ACTION preserves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand, and ESCALATE holds the disputed amount rather than collecting or refunding it. Only FULL_REFUND or PARTIAL_REFUND would take money out of the fare, and neither is available on an uncorroborated, impaired trace.

No billing-integrity or pass-through correction can be carved out of this fare on the rider's behalf. The fare breakdown reconciles to the 26.73 charged: erp_gantries is empty, tolls and ERP are 0.00, the airport surcharge line is 0.00, the platform fee is 0.80, and there is no charge line for a gantry the trace never crosses and no surcharge on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is nothing to refund under POL-RD-09(4), and no standalone pass-through correction exists to add to any distance refund.
